Name: Tektronix TDS2024 (IEEE-488.2/SCPI-style, via TDS2CMAX GPIB/RS-232 module; NOT the TDS2024B)
Notes: Built from docs/devices/tektronix-tds2024/programming-manual.md (Tektronix part 071-1075-03), scoped to a TDS2CMAX rear module over GPIB/RS-232 - NOT the TDS2024B (different hardware/manual) and NOT a TDS2MEM-equipped unit (no CompactFlash file-system commands here). A plain set command gives NO reply at all (success or failure is silent) - always follow with the matching query or check *ESR?/ALLEv? to confirm it took. 9.9E37 is the sentinel for 'no valid measurement value' from MEASUrement/CURSor queries - pair those with *ESR?/ALLEv? too. Concatenating multiple commands with ';' needs a leading ':' before every command whose header differs from the previous one, and a ':' must NEVER precede a '*'-prefixed common command; ID?/*IDN? must be last in a concatenated message (event 440 otherwise). RS-232 accepts CR/LF/CRLF/LFCR as input regardless of RS232:TRANsmit:TERMinator, which controls only what the scope sends (default LF, matching this profile's Terminator). Synchronizing with a long-running operation (*CAL?, single-sequence acquisition, HARDCopy STARt) needs *WAI, polling BUSY?, or *OPC?/*OPC - the vendor manual recommends *OPC? over polling ACQuire:STATE?/TRIGger:STATE?. RS-232 hardware and software flow control are mutually exclusive - disable soft flagging before any binary transfer (a binary CURVe? or a BMP hard copy) since a stray XON/XOFF byte in binary data stalls the link.
